content.thinking:
I'm working through how the loft's width axis relates to the path direction—trying to pin down which local axis (rx) maps to the binormal when the tangent runs along world X, and how that resolves with the up-vector convention in a right-handed system.

Now I'm planning the lower jaw as a loft along a diagonal path from the hinge, setting station widths and heights that taper toward the tip, and sketching out teeth placement—upper fangs and smaller teeth positioned along the jaw's width profile, with lower teeth angled upward from the jaw's top line.

For the eyes, I'm positioning dark socket spheres and glowing inner spheres on the sides of the cranium, checking that the glow spheres protrude slightly past the skull surface so they stay visible given the cranium's width at that x-position.

Now I'm working out the brow ridge as a swept capsule shape angled outward and downward for an overhanging effect, adding brow spikes, then setting up the horn geometry as bezier curves mirrored left and right, and starting to assemble the bone vertex lists using helper cylinder functions.

I'm building gold decorative collars using lathe geometry and cylinder/torus shapes, merging them into the gold parts group, then adding small octahedron gems for the teal highlights with a glow effect applied through a helper function. I'm also starting to sketch out the flame SVG path for the card textures...

Now I'm designing the wisp ghost card with a trailing tail, hollow dark eyes for contrast against the glow, and a teal-to-mint color gradient, plus a rune ring design with stroked circles for the glyph border.

Still writing glyph patterns...

Now I'm thinking about plinth decoration, considering adding a decal emblem on multiple faces using an octagonal lathe geometry, but I need to figure out the angular positions of face centers before placing them.

Working out the rotation so each panel face centers correctly, then using position and normal to compute angle-based paint patterns independent of geometry.

I'm planning a gold-framed decal with an original soul-skull rune (avoiding any named character likeness) placed on the forward face, then designing the tiered cylinder dimensions—body, gold trim band, and cap—with specific radii and heights for each layer.

I'm working out mottled stone paint patterns for the plinth, blending violet and dark ink tones to texture each tier's surface.

I'm adding small ivory fangs at the plinth's corners and a ring of flame cards emerging from the rune circle at the base, keeping the overall part count around 200. Checking the total height against a real scythe's proportions, I'm weighing whether the fantasy scale feels too exaggerated.

Now I'm working out the gold trim sweep along the blade's spine, computing a tapering radius curve and building the path from spine points, then adding ivory spikes angled outward along the spine using blended normal and tangent directions.

I'm skipping heel decoration for now and moving to finalize the painted merged geometry attached to the root joint, then setting up card frames for flame effects along the spine with outward-and-upward directional bias.

Working out the card orientation so the flames face toward the viewer while curling along the blade's tangent direction, adjusting flow and cross settings so they read as edge-lit flames rather than flat facing cards.

Adding eye glow spheres with small upward flame cards, nasal and brow flame details, then moving to write the file. I'm also sketching vertebra helper geometry for sections A and D, with centrum cylinders, inter-disc tube cores, and spinous process cones at specific offsets and angles.

For section D I'm adding transverse processes on both sides plus tiny rib stubs for a dragon-bone look, scaling vertebrae larger near the top. I'm defining the core tube as a sweep between two points with bone-dark coloring, a grip wrap sweep section, gold collar rings at several y-positions, and a neck cap near the top, then setting up the wrap pattern math for painting the grip texture.

Now I'm designing the nib as a curved sweep with a tapered radius, a leather-wrap paint pattern, and a gold clamp ring attaching it to the snath, plus a gold ball and gem at the handle end. For the soul cage, I'm laying out four ribs spaced 72 degrees apart as tapered curved sweeps bulging outward from the shaft and tapering back in near the top.

I'm placing a glowing teal orb sphere around the snath partway up, letting the shaft pass through it opaquely, then adding a gold collar at the neck where the snath meets the skull base, figuring out how the cranium geometry sits relative to the top of the shaft around y≈1.9-2.0.

Now I'm working out positions for a sagittal crest of small spikes along the cranium's midline, angled back and up with varying lengths, plus planning thin cheek frill fins extruding from the skull sides.

Still plotting fin outline points...

I'll give the fins a simple flat color with a teal outline, using "#7a45e0" for the glow tone. For the plinth I'm adding rune circle decals and plaques, leaving the floor plain, then moving on to the soul wisp cards.

Six flame cards get placed at the plinth runes, and I'm adding three small bone talons ring around the plinth front. I'm plotting their curve as a path from base to tip using coordinate pairs for radius and height, with tapering radii and rounded root caps hidden in the plinth. Now I'm ready to write the full code in one pass.

Writing talon and decal code...

Since the blade is planar, the decal should drape fine despite the curvature. I'm checking rune placement at t=0.40, 0.52, 0.64, 0.76, recalculating panel and rune widths at each point to confirm the decal sizing stays consistent — narrowing slightly near the tip but still fitting within the 0.06 panel.

Now I'm setting up the glow effects for both the eye and the decal parts, then adding a rune ring texture to the plinth top using a circle geometry facing upward. I'm working out the plinth's center position and rotation, and thinking through how surface normals should drive paint orientation for wall-like parts.

I'm computing panel line positions based on angular distance from octagonal vertices versus face centers, using a modular angle calculation to find edge proximity for inset panel detailing, then applying similar panel plaque decals to the T3 tier body on all four sides.

Now I'm placing eight rune plaques around the T3 body at 45-degree intervals, positioning each one at the octagon's apothem distance and orienting it to face outward, with textures showing a dark violet rounded rectangle, gold border, and glowing teal sigil design.

I'm also setting up the gold trim for T2 and the corner teeth, then defining the bone paint shader using a mottled countershading technique that darkens the underside based on surface normal, and a similar skull paint variant with a teal tint near the brow.
